outcome: incidence of short-term complications (neonatal pulmonary hemorrhage, neonatal shock, late-onset diseases, retinopathy of prematurity requiring intervention, intracranial hemorrhage (grade 3 or 4), periventricular leukomalacia, neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (>=stage II), moderate to severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia)
persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN)
cohort: The study included 434 preterm infants with gestational age less than 34 weeks who received inhaled nitric oxide therapy in eight Class A tertiary hospitals in China between January 2013 and December 2022.
finding: The rate of iNO usage was highest in extremely preterm infants, but iNO failed to improve the clinical outcome of extremely preterm infants with refractory hypoxemia, and there was no significant difference in its therapeutic effect among preterm infants with different gestational ages.
gest_age: < 34 weeks (divided into 24-27 weeks, 28-31 weeks, and 32-33 weeks)
